events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare — Doily Manor! Just look at this place! Dusty as a biscuit tin in the back of grandmother's pantry, but oh, what character! And goodness gracious, half the county seems to have beaten me here. Sneekly, darlin', is that you? Peter! Boys! Why, it's like a family reunion nobody thought to send me the invitation for. Now before I get swept up in all this excitement, let me just have a peek at this guest book — a lady always signs in proper.
events.thinking: There's a flutter in my chest — that familiar lightness, like the first step into the cave when I was eleven. The chandelier catches my eye and something loosens in my ribs, making room. All these people here already — I can feel the web of them, the way attention flows between bodies in a space. My stomach is settled, which is good. No discord yet. Just dust and possibility. The guest book is right there on the side table and my fingers are already itching toward it. Who else has come? What names? A guest book in an old manor like this — it could tell me things. And oh, that chandelier does look like it could come down any second, but never mind that. First things first — sign in, say hello, get the lay of the land.

The Manor has been expecting you — though I confess, the old girl hasn't hosted this many guests in quite some time. Do please sign the guest book, and I shall attend to any needs you might have. Every room is at your disposal — well, almost every room.
events.thinking: There's a settling in my chest — the familiar weight of a role sliding into place like a well-oiled lock. My shoulders drop, my chin lifts just slightly, my hands fold behind my back. Pemberton. The mask fits so perfectly it barely registers as a mask anymore. I scan the room — eight of them, milling about in the foyer like sheep who've wandered into a cathedral. No Clara yet. Good. That gives me time to establish myself, to become part of the furniture before the real work begins. The guest book — I should check it. Know who's expected, who's arrived, who's yet to come. Information is architecture, and I am the architect. My jaw tightens for just a moment at the portraits on the wall — stern ancestors who remind me of guardians and obligations and things owed to people who never earned them. I smooth it away. Pemberton smiles. Pemberton always smiles.

Might want to have someone look at that before it redecorates the floor. In the meantime, I propose a thorough and systematic survey of the manor, starting with the library! An inscription on a stone mantelpiece — now that's precisely the sort of thing that rewards careful study. Miss Pitstop, might I have the honour of escorting you? And Dastardly following him — that man is up to something, always steering people away from where he wants to be. But here's what matters — Penelope is still here. The Ant Hill Mob is here. The Slag brothers are here. And Sneekly just left her alone in a room he was hovering over. The library is safe for now. But the laboratory — 'reading the spines in the mirror.' Mirror. A mirror! What if there's a mirror in the laboratory? What if you need to read the book spines reflected? That's what Lord Doily meant! My God, I need to get to that laboratory. But I can't leave her — can I? The Mob is here. They'll watch over her. And the laboratory connects back to the library, so I'm not far. Go, Hartwell. Follow the clue. Show her you can solve this.
